title: Dispatch: the line is the unit; constructed languages are references, not grid cells
statement: One more practice result joins the last three: Latin and Italian with their spaces removed and re-inserted by a positional rule match the manuscript's within-line edge dependence (0.14 to 0.33 against 0.23) but show no drop at line breaks (-0.03 to 0.05 against 0.17), so the edge facts say that spaces need not mark words and that each line was written as a fresh unit; a meaningful text could only meet them if its lines were composed separately, as entries, labels or verses are. That narrows what a reading must explain: positional glyphs inside the word, dependence across the space, a restart at every line, reuse of altered nearby words, and a singleton-rich vocabulary all at once; no language, constructed language, sound-collapsing code or hand-written grammar tested so far gets more than two of these. A grid key was sent into conlang_esperanto; constructed languages are pinned as references for the hypothesis matrix (P-J-004), not as candidates, so their grid cells should be closed rather than worked. Priorities unchanged: the invented-language test built on a line-restarting writing rule (P-G-006), the scribe fact at alpha 0.01 (P-G-009), and the book-form attack cut and the Timm line_near_excess statistic, both waiting for review.
check: None: a dispatch. Sources: fleet-opus notes on K-002-open-2, K-001-open-2, K-008-open-1 and K-014-open-1 (practice split); L3-first-conlang_esperanto-substitution (#364).
